issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` may match non-time substrings inside identifiers or strings, causing unnecessary slow-path parsing.
issues.detail: Values like `content: "1ms-old"` or custom identifiers containing `1s` will pass the fast check and fall back to full valueParser parsing. This is safe (correctness preserved) but slightly reduces the optimization's effectiveness. Consider a tighter regex or word-boundary anchoring if profiling shows it matters.

issues.description: No test added to confirm the fast-path skip behavior or guard against future regressions.
issues.detail: The changeset documents the perf fix but no new test asserts that values without time units short-circuit, nor that values with time units still get parsed. A simple unit test covering both branches would protect the optimization from being silently broken by a future regex change.

issues.description: Changeset wording is terse and lacks user-facing context.
issues.detail: "Fixed: `time-min-milliseconds` performance" doesn't convey impact (e.g., "avoids parsing declaration values that contain no time units"). Stylelint changesets typically include enough detail for the changelog reader to understand the fix.

review.summary: This is a clean, minimal performance optimization: a cheap regex pre-check (`/\\dm?s/i`) short-circuits the expensive `valueParser` call when the declaration value contains no time units. The regex correctly captures CSS time syntax (digit followed by `s` or `ms`, case-insensitive) and preserves prior behavior in all edge cases I considered (negative times, decimals, var() references, unitless zero). No correctness or security concerns. Minor suggestions only: tighter regex scoping, a unit test pinning the fast path, and a more descriptive changeset entry.
